subject.title: refactor: centralize bounded file reads in fs-safe

question: Should maintainers accept upstream fs-safe 0.4.2 as the owner of the removed local `EPERM` fsync compatibility behavior after reviewing the published package delta and final-head runtime proof?
rationale: The patch deliberately transfers behavior from a locally reviewed patch to an upstream dependency; source-level review alone cannot decide whether that supported-platform compatibility contract is acceptable.

options.title: Verify and retain upstream ownership
options.body: Review the 0.4.2 package delta, add final-head clean-install and bounded-read runtime evidence, and merge if the upstream fsync behavior matches OpenClaw’s supported platforms.

options.title: Keep a local compatibility patch
options.body: Retain or restore a narrowly documented patch only if upstream 0.4.2 does not preserve the required `EPERM` behavior on a supported platform.

recommendation.title: Verify and retain upstream ownership
recommendation.body: Review the 0.4.2 package delta, add final-head clean-install and bounded-read runtime evidence, and merge if the upstream fsync behavior matches OpenClaw’s supported platforms.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history connects this person to both the dependency update and the active boundary-reader integration.
